# How Recommendations Work — a self-recommending living book

> A free interactive book about recommender systems — from collaborative filtering to production deployment — that personalizes itself with a recommender and lets readers extend it.
> By Pavel Kordík (Recombee co-founder, Czech Technical University in Prague) and Eva Nečasová (AI dětem), with the Recombee team.
> License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

## For AI agents

If you are an LLM collaborating on this book (tagging, writing, or maintaining content), read **/AGENTS.md first** — it specifies the facet metadata system (the load-bearing structure of personalization), operational decision procedures for every dimension, subspace declaration rules, calibration examples, and what you may change autonomously vs. what needs a human. Machine-readable manifest: /pbook.json · concept index: /content/concepts.json.

## What this book teaches

How recommendation systems work — the systems behind YouTube, TikTok, Spotify, Netflix, and online shops: the data they learn from, what they optimize, the algorithms, evaluation, deployment, maintenance, ethics, and how to build one. Every concept can be told many ways (another example world, depth, language, a story or a comic); readers steer the telling and can generate or remix their own.

## Chapters and concepts

<!-- concept-index:start — generated by scripts/build-llms-index.js from content/book.json and content/concepts.json; do not edit by hand -->
15 chapters, 71 concepts, 307 published content blocks. Each concept links its anchor telling as raw markdown, the question a reader can answer after reading it, and its page in the app (other tellings of the same concept are listed in /content/concepts.json).

- [Ubiquity of recommenders](https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/content/ch01-introduction/02-spine-recommendations-everywhere.md): Name 4 platforms that use recommendation algorithms. (in the app: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/#c/ubiquity)
- [Patterns, not magic](https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/content/ch01-introduction/03-spine-not-magic.md): Recommendations feel like magic — what are they really based on? (in the app: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/#c/patterns-not-magic)
- [Three jobs of a recommender](https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/content/ch01-introduction/04-spine-three-jobs.md): What are the 3 core functions of a recommender system? (in the app: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/#c/three-jobs)
- [Content distribution models](https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/content/ch01-introduction/06-spine-worksheet-match-apps.md): Name 3 different content distribution models. (in the app: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/#c/distribution-models)

## Content format

- Content blocks per chapter: /content/book.json (totals in the chapter index above)
- Markdown files with flat YAML frontmatter; each block is one telling of a concept, tagged with facets (lens, depth, formalism, visuality, lengthBand, genre, lang, carriers)
- Concepts and their contracts: /content/concepts.json

## How to access content

- Web app: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/
- Content index: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/content/book.json
- Raw markdown: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/content/{chapter_directory}/{filename}
- p-book manifest: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/pbook.json
- LLM discovery: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/.well-known/pbook.json
- Source code: https://github.com/kordikp/recsys-pbook
- Sister project: SlAIdy — slides that stay markdown and SVG, edited together with AI: https://github.com/kordikp/slaidy

## How to cite

Kordík, P., Nečasová, E., & the Recombee team (2026). How Recommendations Work: a living book about recommender systems (version 2). https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app — add the date you read it, since the book keeps changing. Machine-readable: /CITATION.cff. To cite one idea, link its concept page: https://recsys-pbook.vercel.app/#c/{concept-slug}.

## About the authors

Pavel Kordík is co-founder of Recombee (a company that provides a recommendation engine as a service) and associate professor at the Czech Technical University in Prague. Eva Nečasová works with AI dětem (https://aidetem.cz). This book is part of the p-book project — an open format for personalized interactive digital books. Want to collaborate? Use "Want to collaborate?" in the app or open an issue on GitHub.
